Oil fell on Friday after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before November's midterms, citing “productive discussions” with Tehran, with WTI near ~$90 and Brent ~$103; the IEA also agreed to accelerate oil-reserve releases. Tech rebounded and equity futures firmed ~+0.4%. But three live wires remain: the US–Iran war drags on with Hormuz-shipping thinned, the 10Y sits near ~5.2% just off 24-year highs, and year-ahead inflation expectations hit 3.9%, the highest since 2023, keeping Fed policy hawkish. Gold firmed toward ~$4,207. The scanner boarded two bullish Type C breakouts — EWZ (Grade A) and FRO (Grade B) — but this is still a headline-and-rate tape a Sniper trades only small and validated.
focus.notdown: Brazil / EM & tanker-shipping names (EWZ, FRO) are the scanner's two boarded breakouts — EWZ rode a strong EM/commodity bid to a new 52-week high on 7.8x volume, and FRO (an oil-tanker owner) printed a same-day breakout on war-driven tanker-rate strength. Both are real technical breakouts, but FRO's bid is a war-premium shipping trade that reverses on de-escalation — and oil just eased on exactly that. Megacap tech & AI/semis rebounded, but that's stretched momentum, not a named catalyst. Validate hard at 9:35.
focus.notup: Airlines (DAL/UAL/AAL) are pressured — Delta missed for the first time in two years and slashed its 2026 profit outlook as fuel costs stay high. The fundamental lean is down, but shorting into a day where oil is falling (easing the fuel-cost thesis) and a possible de-escalation squeeze carries its own violent-reversal risk. Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.2%. The disciplined answer on a RED day is to sell nothing new unless it's a validated A-grade breakout, half size.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~49 sits at the top of MILD and P(≥1% gap) at 36% is just above the 35% trigger — the gap trigger alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military conflict (even with de-escalation hopes) stacked on a bond market near 5.2% 24-year-high yields and 3.9% inflation expectations is an unscheduled, open-ended tail. The scanner did board two bullish breakouts — EWZ (Grade A) and FRO (Grade B) — but FRO's war-premium bid can reverse on one peace headline. Trade only validated A-grade at half size, or stand down and push DTE past the headline window. Cash is a position today.

risks: US–Iran war & the de-escalation head-fake — Trump ruled out a strike before the November midterms and oil eased, but the war is still active and Hormuz shipping is thinned. Any reversal of that pledge — or a fresh strait incident — gaps the whole tape and spikes crude. The number-one thing to watch.

Bond yields & inflation expectations — the 10Y sits near ~5.2%, just off 24-year highs, and year-ahead inflation expectations hit 3.9%, the highest since 2023. Fed minutes keep a year-end hike alive; any renewed yield pop hits REITs, utilities, housing and small caps hardest.

Oil is now two-sided — WTI near ~$90 and Brent ~$103 eased on de-escalation and IEA reserve releases, but the war premium isn't gone. A re-escalation sends crude (and jet fuel) back up and feeds inflation fear; continued easing pressures the FRO/energy war trade.

Delta miss & airline read-through — Delta missed for the first time in two years and cut its 2026 EPS outlook to $5.10–$5.60 as fuel costs outpace fares. Single-stock and sector gap risk for airlines; watch the ripple into UAL/AAL.

Big banks ~10/13–14 + CPI/PPI — Q3 bank season opens next week into a 24-year-high bond market, stacking macro and single-stock risk. Keep every spread clear of its name's print and short-dated enough to clear the data.
